description: We are chemical engineering students with a background in thermodynamics, reaction kinetics, and transport phenomena. We're looking for teammates skilled in Python, data analysis, machine learning, or visualization. We can help interpret the physics, while you bring new ways to explore and present the data. You'll gain experience applying data science to engineering questions, and we'll learn from your analytical approach. Let's exchange ideas, learn from each other, and build together.
summary:
Flame Atlas is an interactive, AI-assisted dashboard that connects NASA combustion research to fire-safety questions for human space exploration. Users select a habitat scenario, ask questions in natural language, and explore ranked literature, concise summaries, and linked experimental data and model visualizations.

The platform addresses the challenge by connecting NASA PSI investigations and supporting research to fire prevention, smoke detection, and suppression. It preserves experimental context, including fuel, oxygen concentration, pressure, airflow, and gravity, while providing references to original sources.

Flame Atlas helps engineers, researchers, and students compare findings, identify evidence gaps, and develop focused design and testing questions. Its intended impact is to support informed fire-safety research for spacecraft, space stations, and future lunar and Martian habitats. By making scientific evidence easier to explore alongside its uncertainties and applicability limits, the project helps users turn NASA research into ideas for safer human exploration.
details:
Project Overview

Flame Atlas is an interactive, AI-assisted dashboard that connects NASA combustion research to fire-safety questions for spacecraft, space stations, and future lunar and Martian habitats. It helps researchers, engineers, and students explore how experimental findings can inform fire prevention, smoke detection, and suppression.

How It Works

Users begin by selecting a habitat scenario and asking a question in natural language. The system retrieves and ranks relevant research across solid materials, gaseous fuels, liquid fuels, and smoke from electrical overheating.

It then brings together a concise explanation, supporting literature, and linked experimental or model-based charts. Interactive controls let users explore available parameters while keeping the associated research conditions and limitations visible.

NASA Data and Supporting Evidence

The project combines NASA PSI investigations with related publications and fire-safety references. Its current evidence collection includes 370 indexed literature records, 525 dataset Markdown notes, and 29 source-linked experiment and model chart views.

The structured notes connect experimental conditions, measured quantities, published conclusions, and potential fire-safety implications. The AI receives relevant retrieved papers and dataset notes, and its generated summaries undergo checks for valid source identities, supporting evidence spans, and numerical claims.

Results retain links to original NASA, NTRS, and DOI sources so users can examine the underlying evidence.

Creativity and Fire-Safety Applications

Our creative approach connects habitat scenarios, research questions, experimental evidence, and engineering ideas within one interface.

  • A question about material flammability can lead to relevant flame-spread studies and material-screening considerations.
  • A smoke-detection question can lead to aerosol measurements and detector-related findings.
  • Suppression questions can reveal extinction mechanisms, experimental boundaries, and opportunities for further testing.

Connecting these perspectives helps users identify relationships across investigations and formulate more focused research or design questions.

Tools and Technologies

  • We developed the backend in Python 3.12, using NumPy and SciPy for numerical processing and existing model calculations.
  • The browser interface uses HTML, CSS, and JavaScript.
  • GPT-6.1 Sol, accessed through the OpenAI Responses API, supports question interpretation and summaries grounded in retrieved material.
  • GitHub supports version control, while Docker and Cloudflare Workers with Containers host the Python application and web interface.

Design Considerations and Intended Impact

Our team considered differences in fuel identity, material properties, geometry, oxygen concentration, pressure, airflow, gravity, and measurement methods when organizing comparisons. Source traceability, missing data, uncertainty, and usability guided the dashboard design.

Microgravity evidence informs questions about future habitats, with transfer to partial-gravity environments treated as an area requiring further validation.

The intended impact is to make NASA research easier to investigate, compare, and apply to promising fire-safety research directions, follow-up experiments, and engineering development.
